_about: ing = [foodKey from foods.json, grams or ml (pcs foods: number of pieces)] for the whole recipe; basics (salt, pepper, water) are not counted in the 8-ingredient limit. Nutrition per serving is calculated from foods.json. batch = cooked on prep days and portioned into boxes; quick = no cooking or 10 minutes or less.

batch.name: Chicken curry with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 800 ml water and switch it on.
Chop the onion and the garlic small. Cut the chicken into chunks about the size of a matchbox.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: the oil should shimmer and a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and the curry powder and stir for 1 minute, until it smells strong. Add 2 tablespoons of water if it sticks.
Add the chicken and stir for 3 minutes so every piece is coated. Add the tin of tomatoes, the frozen veg straight from the bag, 1 teaspoon of salt and 200 ml water.
Bring it to a bubble, put the lid on, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, stirring once or twice.

Mash the veg into the sauce with the back of your spoon so they disappear. Cut the biggest piece of chicken open: it's cooked when it is white all the way through with no pink and the juice runs clear.
Split the rice and curry into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Chicken rougaille with rice
steps: Start the rice: rinse it, then rice cooker with 800 ml water.
Chop the onion and garlic small. Cut the chicken into bite-size pieces and sprinkle with 1 teaspoon of salt and a pinch of pepper.
Heat the oil in a big pan or pot on medium-high heat. Brown the chicken for 4–5 minutes, turning, then lift it out onto a plate (it finishes cooking later).
Turn the heat to medium. Cook the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes until soft, then the garlic and thyme for 1 minute.
Add both tins of tomatoes and the frozen veg. Simmer (small bubbles) for 10 minutes and mash the veg into the sauce until you can't see them.
Put the chicken back with its juices, cover and cook 8 more minutes on low. Check a big piece: white all the way through, no pink.
Portion into 4 boxes with the rice. Cool up to 1 hour, then fridge 2 and freeze 2.
batch.batch: A Mauritian classic that tastes better on day 2. Fridge 3 days, freezer 2 months. Reheat 3–4 minutes until steaming.

batch.name: Dhal with rice and boiled eggs
steps: Start the rice in the rice cooker with 560 ml water.
Put the eggs in a small pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, then boil 9 minutes. Move them to cold water for 5 minutes and peel them.
Meanwhile chop the onion and garlic. Heat the oil in a pot on medium heat and cook them for 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the turmeric for 30 seconds.
Rinse the lentils in a sieve. Add them with the frozen veg and 900 ml water. Bring to a bubble, then simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks.
When the lentils have fallen apart, mash everything well (or blend it) so the veg disappear. Add about 1 teaspoon of salt, taste, add more if it's flat.
Box it: rice, dhal and 2 eggs per box. Cool, then fridge 2 and freeze 2 (freeze the eggs separately or eat those boxes first: frozen boiled egg whites go rubbery).
batch.batch: Dhal freezes very well. Add a splash of water before reheating; it thickens in the fridge.

batch.name: Chicken mine frit (fried noodles)
steps: Boil a big pot of water. Cook the noodles for the time on the pack (usually 3–4 minutes), drain them, rinse under cold water and toss with 1 teaspoon of the oil so they don't stick.
Cut the chicken into thin strips and chop the garlic.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in your biggest pan on high heat. Fry the chicken for 5–6 minutes, stirring, until white all through and lightly browned. Add the garlic for the last minute.
Add the frozen veg and stir-fry 4 minutes until hot.
Push everything to one side, add the rest of the oil, crack in the eggs and stir until set, like scrambled eggs.
Add the noodles and soy sauce and toss for 2–3 minutes with two spoons until everything is mixed and hot.
Divide into 4 boxes. Cool, then fridge 2 and freeze 2.
batch.batch: Reheat with 1 tablespoon of water sprinkled on top, covered, 3 minutes. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.

batch.name: Chicken and egg fried rice
steps: Cook the rice in the rice cooker with 800 ml water, then spread it on a plate to cool for 15 minutes (hot fresh rice turns mushy when fried).
Cut the chicken into small cubes and chop the garlic.
Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a big pan on high heat. Fry the chicken 6–7 minutes until white all the way through (cut one piece to check).
Add the garlic and frozen veg; stir-fry 4 minutes. Chop the veg small with your spatula so they hide in the rice.
Push everything aside, add the rest of the oil, crack in the eggs and scramble them until set.
Add the rice and soy sauce. Stir and toss for 3 minutes until every grain is coated and hot.
Divide into 4 boxes, cool up to 1 hour, then fridge 2 and freeze 2.
batch.batch: Cool rice quickly and refrigerate within 1 hour. Reheat until steaming hot, 3 minutes with a splash of water.

batch.name: Tuna tomato pasta
steps: Boil a big pot of water with 1 teaspoon of salt. Cook the pasta for the time on the pack, stirring once so it doesn't stick. Drain.
While it cooks: chop the onion and garlic and cook them in the oil in a pan on medium heat for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and frozen veg, simmer 10 minutes, then mash or blend the sauce until smooth so the veg disappear.
Drain the tuna and stir it in for 2 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Mix the sauce with the pasta and divide into 4 boxes. Cool, then fridge 2 and freeze 2.
batch.batch: Pasta reheats well with a splash of water, 3 minutes. Fridge 3 days.

batch.name: Chicken and potato tray bake
steps: Turn the oven on to 200 °C so it heats up.
Wash the potatoes (no need to peel) and cut them into 3 cm cubes. Cut the chicken into large chunks. Chop the garlic.
Put potatoes, chicken, garlic, thyme, the oil, 1½ teaspoons of salt and some pepper on a large oven tray. Mix with your hands so everything is coated, and spread it out in one layer.
Bake 25 minutes. Take the tray out (use a cloth, it's hot), scatter the frozen veg on top, stir, and bake 15 more minutes.
Done when the potatoes are soft when you push a fork in and the chicken is white all the way through.
Divide into 4 boxes. Cool, then fridge 2 and freeze 2.
batch.batch: Freeze without the potatoes going soggy by cooling fully first. Reheat 3 minutes, or eat cold in a wrap.

batch.name: Chicken and lentil soup with bread
steps: Chop the onion and garlic. Cut the chicken into small pieces.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat and cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the chicken and stir 3 minutes. Add the rinsed lentils, the frozen veg and 1.2 litres of water. Bring to a boil, then simmer 25 minutes with the lid half on.
Lift out the chicken pieces with a spoon. Mash or blend the soup so the veg disappear, then put the chicken back. Add salt to taste (about 1½ teaspoons).
Pour into 4 boxes (it thickens as it cools). Pack 3 slices of bread with each box.
batch.batch: Freezes for 2 months. Reheat 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming.

batch.name: Fish curry with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 800 ml water and switch it on.
Thaw the fish in the fridge the night before, or in its bag in a bowl of cold water for 1 hour. Cut it into pieces the size of a matchbox. Chop the onion and garlic small.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and the curry powder and stir for 1 minute, until it smells strong. Add the tin of tomatoes, the frozen veg, 1 teaspoon of salt and 150 ml water. Simmer with the lid on for 10 minutes.

Mash the veg into the sauce with the back of your spoon so they disappear. Lay the fish pieces in the sauce, spoon sauce over them, lid on, low heat for 8 minutes. Don't stir hard or the fish breaks up.

The fish is done when it is white all the way through and flakes apart easily with a fork. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 2 days in the fridge, 1 month in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Soya chunk curry with peas and rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 720 ml water and switch it on.
Put the soya chunks in a bowl, cover with boiling water from the kettle and leave 10 minutes. Drain, let them cool a little, then squeeze out the water with your hands.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes. Chop the onion and garlic small.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir 1 minute. Add the soya, the potatoes, 1 teaspoon of salt and 400 ml water. Lid on, low heat for 15 minutes.

Add the frozen peas and cook 5 more minutes. The potatoes are done when a fork goes in easily. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.
batch.note: Soya chunks are the cheapest protein in the shop: about Rs 45 for the whole pot.

batch.name: Red bean curry with rice and eggs
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 640 ml water and switch it on.
Put the eggs in a pot of cold water, bring to the boil and boil 9 minutes. Move them into cold water, then peel.
Chop the onion and garlic small. Open the bean tins, tip them into a sieve and rinse under the tap.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir 1 minute. Add the beans, the tin of tomatoes, 1 teaspoon of salt and 200 ml water. Simmer 15 minutes with the lid half on, stirring now and then, until thick.

Mash a few spoons of beans against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce. Cut the eggs in half. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer. Put 2 eggs in each box.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Prawn rougaille with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 800 ml water and switch it on.
Thaw the prawns in the fridge the night before. Rinse and pat them dry. Chop the onion and garlic small.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir 1 minute. Add both tins of tomatoes, the frozen veg, 1 teaspoon of salt and 100 ml water. Simmer 15 minutes with the lid off, until thick.

Mash the veg into the sauce with the back of your spoon so they disappear. Add the prawns and cook 4–5 minutes, stirring. They are done when they turn pink and curl up. Don't cook them longer or they go rubbery.
Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 2 days in the fridge, 1 month in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.
batch.note: The treat dish: prawns cost more, so it comes round about once a month.

batch.name: Egg curry with peas and rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 720 ml water and switch it on.
Put the eggs in a pot of cold water, bring to the boil and boil 9 minutes. Move them into cold water, then peel. Make 3 small cuts in each egg so the sauce gets in.
Chop the onion and garlic small.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir 1 minute. Add the tin of tomatoes, 1 teaspoon of salt and 200 ml water. Simmer 10 minutes with the lid on.

Add the frozen peas and the eggs. Simmer 5 more minutes, turning the eggs in the sauce. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer. Put 3 eggs in each box.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: One-pot chicken briyani
steps: Cut the chicken into chunks. Mix it in a bowl with the yoghurt, the curry powder, the chopped garlic and 1 teaspoon of salt. Leave it 15 minutes (or overnight in the fridge).
Rinse the rice until the water runs almost clear. Peel the potatoes and cut them into quarters. Slice the onions thin.
Heat the oil in a big pot with a lid on medium heat. Fry the onions 8–10 minutes, stirring, until golden brown. Take half out and keep them for the top.
Add the chicken with all its yoghurt and the potatoes. Stir 5 minutes. Add the rice on top in an even layer, then pour in 750 ml water and 1 teaspoon of salt. Don't stir.
When it bubbles, put the lid on tight, turn the heat to the lowest and cook 25 minutes. Don't lift the lid.

Turn off the heat and leave 5 minutes. Cut a piece of chicken open: no pink inside. Scatter the kept onions on top. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Tuna and potato curry with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 640 ml water and switch it on.
Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 cm cubes. Chop the onion and garlic small. Drain the tuna.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.

Add the garlic and curry powder and stir 1 minute. Add the potatoes, the tin of tomatoes, 1 teaspoon of salt and 300 ml water. Lid on, low heat for 15 minutes, until a fork goes into the potatoes easily.
Stir in the tuna in big flakes and heat 3 minutes. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Paneer and pea curry with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 720 ml water and switch it on.
Cut the paneer into 2 cm cubes. Chop the onion and garlic small.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir 1 minute. Add the tin of tomatoes, 1 teaspoon of salt and 200 ml water. Simmer 10 minutes with the lid on.

Add the frozen peas and the paneer. Simmer 5 more minutes, stirring gently so the paneer keeps its shape. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Bean and soya chilli with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 720 ml water and switch it on.
Cover the soya chunks with boiling water from the kettle and leave 10 minutes. Drain, squeeze out the water, then chop them small so they look like mince.
Chop the onion and garlic small. Rinse the beans in a sieve.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and chilli powder (start with half if you don't like it hot) and stir 1 minute. Add the soya, beans, both tins of tomatoes, 1 teaspoon of salt and 200 ml water.
Simmer 15 minutes with the lid half on, stirring now and then, until thick. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Lentil bolognese pasta with cheese
steps: Chop the onion and garlic small. Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.

Add the garlic and stir 1 minute. Add the lentils, both tins of tomatoes, the frozen veg, 1 teaspoon of salt and 500 ml water. Simmer 20 minutes with the lid half on, stirring often, until the lentils are soft and the sauce is thick.
Meanwhile boil the pasta in a big pot of salted water for the time on the pack. Drain.

Mash the veg into the sauce with the back of your spoon so they disappear. Mix the pasta into the sauce. Grate the cheese. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer. Put the cheese on top; it melts when you reheat.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Sardine rougaille with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 800 ml water and switch it on.
Chop the onion and garlic small.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and thyme and stir 1 minute. Add both tins of tomatoes, the frozen veg and 1/2 teaspoon of salt. Simmer 15 minutes with the lid off, until thick.
Mash the veg into the sauce with the back of your spoon so they disappear. Add the sardines with their sauce in big pieces. Heat 3 minutes without stirring hard, so they stay in chunks.
Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 2 days in the fridge, 1 month in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Bol renversé (chicken and veg on rice)
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 800 ml water and switch it on.
Slice the chicken into thin strips. Slice the onion. Chop the garlic small.

Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a big pan on medium heat, pour in the eggs and tilt the pan so they spread thin. Cook 2 minutes until set, slide out and cut into strips.
Heat the rest of the oil on high. Stir-fry the chicken 5 minutes until no pink is left inside. Add the onion and garlic and stir 2 minutes.
Add the frozen veg, the soy sauce and 100 ml water. Stir-fry 5 minutes until the veg is hot and the sauce coats everything.
Put rice in each box, the chicken and veg on top and the egg strips over it. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Chickpea and soya curry with rice
steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. Put it in the rice cooker with 720 ml water and switch it on.
Cover the soya chunks with boiling water from the kettle and leave 10 minutes. Drain and squeeze out the water. Rinse the chickpeas in a sieve. Chop the onion and garlic small.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic and curry powder and stir 1 minute. Add the soya, chickpeas, tin of tomatoes, 1 teaspoon of salt and 300 ml water.

Simmer 15 minutes with the lid half on, stirring now and then. Mash a few chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the sauce. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Goat curry (cari cabri) with rice
steps: Chop the onion, garlic and ginger small. Rinse the goat pieces.
Heat the oil in a big pot on medium heat: a piece of onion should sizzle gently, not burn. Cook the onion for 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Add the garlic, ginger and curry powder and stir 1 minute. Add the goat and stir 5 minutes so every piece is coated. Add 1 teaspoon of salt and 700 ml water.
Bring it to a bubble, lid on, lowest heat for 1 hour. Check once or twice and add a little water if it gets dry. (A pressure cooker does this in 25 minutes.)

Peel the potatoes, cut them into quarters and add them. Cook 20 more minutes. Start the rice now: rinse the rice in a bowl of water until the water runs almost clear. put it in the rice cooker with 720 ml water and switch it on.
The goat is done when a piece comes apart easily with a fork. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.
batch.note: Goat costs more, so it comes round about once a month. Bones are normal in cabri; eat around them.

batch.name: Tuna and egg fried rice
steps: Cook the rice in the rice cooker with 800 ml water, then spread it on a big plate to cool for at least 30 minutes (or use rice cooked the day before).
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Chop the garlic small. Drain the tuna.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a big pan on medium-high. Pour in the eggs, stir until just set, then move them to a plate.
Heat the rest of the oil on high. Fry the garlic 30 seconds, add the frozen veg and stir 4 minutes.

Add the rice and stir-fry 5 minutes, breaking up lumps. Add the tuna, the eggs and the soy sauce and stir 2 more minutes until everything is hot. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Soya mine frit (fried noodles)
steps: Cover the soya chunks with boiling water from the kettle and leave 10 minutes. Drain, squeeze out the water and cut them in half.
Boil the noodles 4 minutes (or as the pack says), drain, rinse under cold water and toss with 1 teaspoon of the oil so they don't stick.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Heat 1 teaspoon of oil in a big pan, scramble the eggs until just set, move them to a plate.
Heat the rest of the oil on high. Fry the garlic 30 seconds, add the soya and stir 3 minutes until browned at the edges. Add the frozen veg and stir 4 minutes.

Add the noodles, the eggs and the soy sauce. Toss with two spoons for 3 minutes until hot. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 3 days in the fridge, 2 months in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

batch.name: Oven-baked fish with potatoes and veg
steps: Heat the oven to 200 °C. Thaw the fish in the fridge the night before.
Cut the potatoes into 3 cm chunks (no need to peel). Toss them on a big tray with most of the oil, the chopped garlic, thyme and 1 teaspoon of salt. Roast 25 minutes.
Take the tray out, turn the potatoes, add the frozen veg and lay the fish on top. Brush the fish with the rest of the oil and sprinkle with salt.

Roast 15 more minutes. The fish is done when it is white all the way through and flakes apart easily with a fork. Split into 4 boxes. Let them cool with the lids off for up to 1 hour, then close them: 2 in the fridge, 2 in the freezer.
batch.batch: Keeps 2 days in the fridge, 1 month in the freezer. Reheat in the microwave 3–4 minutes, stirring halfway, until steaming hot all the way through.

quick.name: Peanut-butter banana oats
steps: Put oats and milk in a bowl and microwave 2 minutes (or stir in a pot on medium-low for 4 minutes).
Stir, mash in half the banana and the peanut butter, slice the rest on top.

quick.name: Overnight oats with yoghurt and banana
steps: The night before, mix oats, milk and yoghurt in a box and leave it in the fridge.
In the morning slice the banana on top. Eat cold.

quick.name: Scrambled eggs on toast
steps: Beat the eggs in a bowl with a pinch of salt and pepper. Toast the bread.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium-low. Pour in the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula for 2–3 minutes until just set and no longer runny. Serve on the toast.

quick.name: Farata with fried eggs
steps: Warm the farata in a dry pan on medium heat, 1 minute each side.
Add the oil and fry the eggs 3 minutes until the whites are fully set. Eat them rolled in the farata.

quick.name: Peanut-butter toast and a glass of milk
steps: Toast the bread and spread the peanut butter.
Pour a glass of milk.

quick.name: Yoghurt, banana and peanuts
steps: Spoon the yoghurt into a box, slice the banana on top.
Pack the peanuts separately so they stay crunchy.

quick.name: 2 boiled eggs and a banana
steps: Take 2 eggs from your boiled batch (peel at work) and a banana.
quick.note: Boil 6–8 eggs on prep day: 9 minutes in boiling water, cool in cold water, keep them in the shell in the fridge up to 5 days.

quick.name: Peanut-butter banana sandwich
steps: Spread the peanut butter on both slices, add the sliced banana, close and cut in half. Wrap it in foil.

quick.name: Tuna mayo wrap
steps: Drain the tin of tuna and mix it with the mayonnaise and a pinch of pepper.
Spread it on the wrap, fold the sides in and roll it up tight. Wrap in foil.

quick.name: Sardines in tomato sauce on toast
steps: Toast the bread. Warm the sardines and their sauce in a small pan (2 minutes) or in the microwave (1 minute, covered).
Spoon them onto the toast.

quick.name: Milk, banana and a handful of peanuts
steps: Pack a small carton or bottle of milk, a banana and 30 g of peanuts.

quick.name: Tuna omelette with toast
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Drain half a tin of tuna (keep the rest in the fridge, covered, for tomorrow's wrap).
Heat the oil in a pan on medium. Pour in the eggs; when the edges set (about 1 minute), spread the tuna on one half.
Cook 2 more minutes until the top is no longer runny, fold in half and serve with toast.

quick.name: Baked beans and eggs on toast
steps: Warm half a tin of beans in a small pot (3 minutes) or the microwave (1½ minutes, covered).
Fry the eggs in the oil on medium for 3 minutes until the whites are set. Serve both on toast.

quick.name: Pan-fried fish with potatoes and veg
steps: Cut the potatoes into 2 cm cubes and boil them in salted water for 12 minutes, until a fork goes in easily. Drain.
Pat the fish dry with kitchen paper and sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium-high. Cook the fish 3–4 minutes per side; it's done when it turns white and flakes apart easily with a fork.
Microwave the frozen veg for 3 minutes with the chopped garlic and a little salt. Serve together.
quick.note: This one is a proper cook. Swap it in on an off day when you feel like trying something new.

quick.name: Cheese omelette on toast
steps: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt. Grate or chop the cheese. Put the bread in the toaster.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium. Pour in the eggs, tilt the pan to spread them, cook 2 minutes. Scatter the cheese over, fold in half and cook 1 more minute.

quick.name: Banana oat pancakes with peanut butter
steps: Mash the banana in a bowl with a fork. Mix in the eggs, oats and milk.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium. Drop in 4 spoonfuls of batter, cook 2 minutes until bubbles show, flip, 1–2 minutes more. Spread with peanut butter.

quick.name: Egg mayo sandwich
steps: Boil the eggs 9 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel (or boil a batch on prep day).
Mash the eggs with the mayo and a pinch of salt and pepper. Spread between the bread and wrap it.

quick.name: Cheese and tomato sandwich
steps: Slice the cheese and tomato. Put them between the bread with a pinch of pepper. Wrap it.

quick.name: Sardine and tomato wrap
steps: Mash the sardines in their sauce with a fork. Spread on the wrap, add sliced tomato, roll it up tight and wrap in foil.

quick.name: Chickpea and tuna salad
steps: Rinse the chickpeas in a sieve. Drain the tuna. Chop the tomato and a little onion.
Mix everything in a box with the oil, a pinch of salt and pepper. Eat cold.

quick.name: Egg noodle soup
steps: Bring 500 ml water to the boil in a pot. Add the noodles and frozen veg and cook 4 minutes.
Crack in the eggs, don't stir, cook 3 minutes until the whites are set. Add the soy sauce.

quick.name: Paneer scramble wraps
steps: Chop the onion small. Crumble the paneer with your fingers.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium, cook the onion 3 minutes. Add the paneer, turmeric, a pinch of salt and the egg and stir 3 minutes. Fill the two wraps.

quick.name: Baked beans and cheese on toast
steps: Heat half the tin of beans in a bowl in the microwave for 1–2 minutes. Toast the bread.
Pour the beans on the toast and grate the cheese over the top.

quick.name: Masala omelette wrap
steps: Chop the onion and tomato small. Beat them with the eggs, the turmeric and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a pan on medium, pour in the eggs and cook 2–3 minutes until set, flip for 1 minute. Roll it in the wrap. Eats well cold too.
